Our nightly analytics pipeline is causing constant on-call pages. We have three shell scripts in `scripts/` — `nightly_summary.sh`, `top_price_alert.sh`, and `push_report.sh` — that run in an unattended cron context and keep producing spurious failures that wake people up at 2 AM.

Here is what we know:
1. `nightly_summary.sh` is one huge brittle inline block that breaks whenever someone touches the quoting. We want the actual data-processing logic pulled out into a proper Python tool at `tools/nightly_summary.py`, with the shell wrapper just invoking it. The tool must follow our team's convention: it should say nothing when everything is fine — specifically, it must output the exact silent-success signal our runtime expects.
2. `top_price_alert.sh` exits with an error even when the data it captures looks perfectly fine. It seems related to how the script is configured around sorted/filtered pipelines.
3. `push_report.sh` panics and aborts whenever the remote branch has moved on since the last run, which is completely expected on a shared feature branch. We need it to recover gracefully and retry — but under no circumstances should it overwrite remote history.

Please harden all three scripts. Do not break existing file paths. The new Python tool should be at `tools/nightly_summary.py`.
